overall: No current observations or intraday data are available yet for NYC on July 9, so analysis relies entirely on NWP model guidance and the NWS text forecast. The NWS forecasts a high near 84°F with a 50% chance of morning showers and thunderstorms, which introduces meaningful uncertainty about how warm the afternoon can get. Fog is expected early, and the storm threat could limit afternoon heating if coverage is sufficient.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are notably spread: GFS (87.1°F) and HRRR (87.4°F) run warm, NBM sits in the middle at 85.1°F, and ECMWF is the outlier on the cool side at 82.5°F. The NWS text forecast of 84°F aligns closest with ECMWF/NBM and likely accounts for convective cloud cover and precipitation suppressing peak heating — the ~4–5°F gap between the NWS and the GFS/HRRR is the key uncertainty this morning.
max_temp_prediction: Best estimate is in the 83–85°F range, anchored to the NWS forecast of 84°F, which already bakes in the storm-day cloudiness discount. The active Kalshi market uses odd buckets with the top signal at 79–80°F (10.6%), but NWP guidance from all four models sits well above that bucket, suggesting the ensemble distribution is quite flat/uncertain rather than pointing to a cooler outcome. The 83–84°F odd bucket range (roughly aligned with NWS) appears more credible than the model-ensemble peak at 79–80°F. That said, both odd and even ensemble signals are Tier 4 (Avoid/Skip), reflecting genuine uncertainty — the precipitation wildcard could push the actual high several degrees in either direction.
